subject: Outcome agreement & acceptance scaffold for ClearView evaluation
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nolan <sara@clearviewhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Outcome agreement & acceptance scaffold for ClearView evaluation

Sara —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a lightweight outcome agreement you can share with stakeholders. The goal is to make evaluation success binary and actionable so procurement, engineering, and the clinical team can align on what “pass” looks like. 

Attached: MAP-draft-v1.xlsx (scaffold)

Key sections (summary):
- Primary outcome: 95%+ accuracy on entity extraction (diagnosis + medication) on the validation set; F1 measured per-entity.
- Stability gate: inference latency p95 <= 350ms on your median payload (avg tokens ~120).
- Safety/QA gate: false-positive rate on sensitive labels <= 1% across sampled cases; manual review plan for edge cases.
- Acceptance tests: 1) 1k randomized validation prompts, 2) 100 red-team adversarial prompts, 3) end-to-end throughput smoke with your VPC network pattern.

Proposed timeline (draft):
- Week 0 (kickoff): install agent, share baseline dataset (you)
- Week 1: run smoke tests, collect perf profile (Redwood)
- Week 2: acceptance test run (joint)
- Week 3: review results, decision call

Open items for you: confirmation of the validation set owner, and any non-negotiable SLOs from procurement/security. If that looks good I’ll update the MAP and push a final to the Drive.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Attachment: MAP-draft-v1.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)

From: Sara Nolan <sara@clearviewhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit@clearviewhealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@clearviewhealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outcome agreement & acceptance scaffold for ClearView evaluation

Vanessa —

Thanks for pulling this together and for the clear structure. A few quick questions from our side before we circulate to the clinical reviewers: 

1) Validation set ownership: clinical analytics will own the gold labels; I’ll confirm a point person (likely Dr. Chen).
2) The latency goal looks reasonable but procurement will want a worst-case (p99) note in the MAP. Can we add p99 <= 650ms (on our peak payloads) as an optional gate?
3) For safety gating: we need a short description of the manual review workflow (who, cadence) — can you sketch?

Procurement looped in to confirm non-technical constraints (data retention, audit log retention).

We’ll review with clinical on Thursday; please share the test cases you plan to run so we can sanity-check the modalities.

Best,
Sara
Director, Clinical Analytics | ClearView Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nolan <sara@clearviewhealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-23T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outcome agreement & acceptance scaffold for ClearView evaluation

Sara — quick follow from the engineering side. A couple clarifications and what we’ll deliver: 

1) Acceptance test artifacts: we’ll provide a CSV of acceptance-test-cases.csv (deterministic pass/fail) and a sample-prompt-pack.jsonl for randomized runs. These are attached.
2) Manual review workflow: propose a weekly 2-hour spot check during the acceptance run. Clinical analytics assigns 2 reviewers; Redwood will provide a lightweight review UI export (CSV with flags). If a case is flagged as high-severity we automatically open an issue with the root case and a transcript.
3) p99 latency: we can include p99 in the MAP as an informational gate — note that p99 is sensitive to tails and test infrastructure; we'll capture both p95 and p99 with configured load.

Acceptance test plan (brief):
- Deterministic run: 1,000 validation prompts against the pinned model version => compute precision/recall/F1 per label
- Adversarial suite: 100 curated prompts focused on ambiguity and red-team patterns (we’ll seed examples with clinical)
- Throughput smoke: burst 50 concurrent sessions for 10 minutes with your network pattern to validate autoscaling and cache behavior

I’ll be on the call Thursday to walk through the CSV and how to interpret the exported results.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Technical CSM | Redwood Inference

Attachment: acceptance-test-cases.csv (csv, 12KB); sample-prompt-pack.jsonl (jsonl, 5MB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nolan <sara@clearviewhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@clearviewhealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-24T11:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outcome agreement & acceptance scaffold for ClearView evaluation

All —

Updated per Ben and Sara: I’ve added p99 as an informational stability gate and sketched the manual review cadence in the MAP. I pushed a new version to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cMAP-Scaffold (MAP-draft-v1 -> MAP-v1.1). Key changes:
- Manual review: 2 clinicians from ClearView, weekly 90-minute session during acceptance week; Redwood will triage flagged items and provide root transcripts within 24 hours of flagging.
- p99 stability note added: p99 <= 650ms (informational; non-blocking unless it correlates with failure modes)
- Test artifacts attached as Ben noted.

Proposed firm timeline (updated):
- Thu 2026-06-24: clinical kickoff (confirm Dr. Chen)
- Mon 2026-06-28: baseline smoke + perf profile collected
- Tue-Wed 2026-06-29/30: deterministic acceptance runs + adversarial suite
- Thu 2026-07-01: review call and decision (accept / request remediation / fail)

Procurement — if you can confirm any contract-level retention or audit requirements by Monday that would be ideal; otherwise we’ll treat them as standard Redwood defaults and document exceptions in the MAP.

I’ll include a DocuSign stub once procurement confirms the MRN data use appendix.

Thanks —
Vanessa
